description: platformAutomerge is deliberately false: main's Repository Ruleset REQUIRES the ci-pass check, and platformAutomerge:true triggers the registration race (native auto-merge can complete in the ~1s window before ci-pass registers, landing a red bump). Do NOT flip it to true — Renovate merges via its own run after re-confirming green. automergeStrategy is 'merge' (NOT 'squash') because the same Ruleset disallows squash merges.

customManagers.description: Update Makefile tool versions via inline renovate comments

packageRules.description: Wait 3 days before automerging major updates
Group GitHub Actions into one PR
Bump Go version in go.mod to latest patch
Group all toolchain pins (Makefile + .mise.toml) into one PR

Hold every mise aqua: tool (github-tags datasource) 3 days so the upstream GitHub Release artifacts mise's aqua: backend installs are published before the PR opens — prevents the tag-before-publish 404 (`mise install` fetches the release, but github-tags sees the tag first). Covers minor/patch bumps that the major-only buffer misses (kapp, k9s, trivy have all hit this).

Hold node to major 24. node is used only by `make renovate-validate`, and renovate@latest requires node ^24.11 while node 25+ dropped the bundled corepack — so an unguarded mise bump to 25/26 would self-break the validate gate.

The Makefile docker-datasource pins (via the custom.regex manager) are version-only — the matchString captures no currentDigest — so config:best-practices' bundled docker:pinDigests generates an unwritable pinDigest update that collides with and SUPPRESSES the version bump (froze mermaid-cli at 11.4.2 while 11.16.0 was available). Disable digest-pinning for them; the version pin is the reproducibility guarantee.

Do NOT digest-pin the project's OWN published images. deploy/*.yaml reference ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>/<binary>:latest by design (imagePullPolicy: Always re-pulls latest on rollout); these are self-published, not upstream deps, and pinning them to a digest would defeat the :latest refresh.

Group the Go toolchain across managers — the go.mod `go` directive (gomod) and the .mise.toml `go` pin (mise) both use the golang-version datasource; grouping them makes a Go bump land as ONE PR so it can't split-deadlock across managers (complements the Makefile check-go-alignment gate).

PlantUML renderer: no automerge — a bump can change PNG bytes, and the hosted bot cannot run `make diagrams` to re-render + commit. A human shepherds each bump (make diagrams, commit PNGs). Own group so this does not disable Toolchain automerge.
